subtopics.title: The Sole Trader and the Elements of the Books

questions.question: A sole trader is legally one person with the business, yet the records separate them because:
options: The law requires two bank accounts
Profit must measure the business itself, not the owner's household — the business entity rule
Sole traders may not own assets

questions.question: Which set correctly names the growing side of each element?
options: Assets and expenses grow on the debit side; liabilities, equity and income on the credit side
Assets grow on the credit side; everything else on the debit side
All elements grow on the debit side
Income grows on the debit side; expenses on the credit side

questions.question: Owner's equity is best described as:
options: The cash in the business bank account
The value of the fixed assets
The owner's interest in the business — capital in, drawings out, profits growing it, losses shrinking it

subtopics.title: The Pipeline Words — Journal to Ledger to Final Accounts

questions.question: The correct order of the recording pipeline is:
options: Journal → ledger → trial balance → final accounts
Ledger → journal → final accounts → trial balance
Trial balance → journal → ledger → final accounts
Final accounts → trial balance → ledger → journal

questions.question: A supplier lists a shelf at R1 000 but invoices the bulk-buying shop at R850. The R150 is:
options: Trade discount — never recorded; the purchase is simply recorded at R850
Discount allowed, recorded as an expense
A settlement discount, recorded when paid

questions.question: A debtor owing R2 000 settles promptly and is allowed R100 off. The R100 is recorded as:
options: Discount allowed — an expense of the business granting it

questions.question: Gross profit and net profit are calculated respectively in the:
options: Trading account and Profit and Loss account
Profit and Loss account and Trading account

questions.question: Financial accounting is characterised by:
options: Forward-looking budgets in any useful format
Reporting the past, by GAAP rules, in standardised statements for outside parties

questions.question: 'Should the shop open a second branch next year?' is answered by:
options: Managerial accounting — forward-looking, for insiders, judged only by usefulness

questions.question: Why does managerial accounting follow no external rulebook?
options: It is illegal to regulate internal reports
Its only test is usefulness to the internal decision-maker; outsiders never rely on it

questions.question: Under the perpetual inventory system, what is recorded at the moment of every sale?
options: Only the sale at selling price
Only the cost of the goods sold
Two things simultaneously: the sale at selling price AND cost of sales moving out of Trading Stock at cost

questions.question: The Trading Stock account's balance at any moment shows:
options: The cost of stock that should be on hand
The selling value of the shelves

questions.question: Records say R48 000 of stock should be on hand; the count finds R46 500. Under the perpetual system this gap is:
options: A named, investigable loss (theft, breakage or error) visible because the records predicted the shelf

questions.question: Zanele puts R60 000 of her savings into the shop's bank account. The concept is:
options: Capital — the owner's contribution into equity

questions.question: The R20 000 borrowed from her uncle for stock is:
options: A liability — the business owes an outsider

questions.question: Her evening notebook of the day's happenings, and her Sunday pages per item, are respectively:
options: The trial balance and the final accounts
The journal (book of first entry) and the ledger (book of accounts)
Source documents and the bank statement

subtopics.title: The Report Card and the Game Plan

questions.question: The bank asking to see last year's performance receives the:
options: Report card — financial accounting's statements, by the rules, for outsiders

questions.question: Zanele's kitchen-table sneaker estimates are the game plan because they are:
options: Forward-looking, free-format, and for her eyes only

questions.question: The four contrast pairs between the branches are:
options: Past/future, outsiders/insiders, rules/freedom, report card/game plan

questions.question: Zanele sells shoes for R500 that cost her R300. At the till, the counter records:
options: A sale of R500 and, simultaneously, R300 leaving Trading Stock as cost of sales

questions.question: Her gross profit on that pair, visible the moment it happens, is:
Under the old periodic way, the December gap of R1 500 would have:
options: Appeared in the Trading Stock account
Hidden inside the year — the missing shoes would simply look like they were sold
